pairs.why: A keeps a fairly high camera with a big tabletop face and the checker top clearly visible like the real card, while B pulls back and flattens the top into a thin sliver with a smaller hero.
A's truss runs near-horizontal with mild perspective and the lamp hangs from it like the real card, while B's truss slants steeply with stronger forced perspective.
A is a near front-on wall clock with visible bezel thickness and a soft wall shadow like the real card, while B stands the clock on a floor line with a ground plane the real card lacks.
A uses a closer, higher camera with a large hero and a foreground crater and pipe for layering, like the real cards, while B is pulled back with a smaller hero in a wider, emptier scene.
A has a near-horizontal truss and a teal blurred background like the real card, though its hanger is boxy, while B's truss is steeply diagonal and shows the top vents from higher up.
B shows more of the seat's top face and a more 3/4 turn like the real chair, while A's seat is nearly edge-on and flat; both have a hard-edged ground slab the real card lacks.
A is turned 3/4 with a dynamic angle like the real hero objects, while B is a symmetric frontal view, though B shows a bit more top face.
B has stronger 3D volume, with foreshortened fins and a nozzle that read as depth like the real submarine and trumpet, while A's fins and body are flatter.
